top_categories.workout_context: 466 miles across 7 consecutive stages. Train the power that still exists after several long days, not merely late in one ride.
Most stages run for hours, and the next start arrives before recovery is complete. Aerobic depth keeps daily work economical for all 7 days.
Back-to-back simulations rehearse pacing, fueling, equipment care, and the overnight reset across Gravel Burn's 7 stages.
Multi-hour Z2 and back-to-back long rides rehearse Gravel Burn's real demand: finish one substantial day, recover, then do it again.
Repeated selection points still arrive on day 7. VO2 work helps cover surges without turning every hard rise into overnight recovery debt.
Stage-race surges push above threshold, then demand recovery while the race keeps moving. Over-unders train that repeatable pattern.
Gravel Burn's fast Great Karoo gravel across a seven-stage forces repeated power changes. Settle immediately after each surge so the cost does not compound across 7 stages.
Climbing must stay repeatable across 7 days. Change cadence and posture without damaging already-tired legs.
Sustained climbs and fast group pressure demand controlled threshold work. Finish each effort without borrowing from tomorrow's stage.
Endurance with controlled intensity spikes mirrors a long stage: economical riding interrupted by climbs, wind, terrain, and pack accelerations.
Strong sub-threshold power lets you climb and pull without repeatedly crossing the line that ruins between-stage recovery.
Low-cadence force keeps climbing torque available when gearing, surface, or late-week fatigue takes away your preferred cadence.

race_overlay.heat: October in Great Karoo, Eastern Cape, South Africa — The current organizer route guide gives an average range of 10-29°C, while the inaugural race produced freezing nights, heat, and a storm severe enough to neutralize racing. Complete heat acclimatization before travel, then reassess fluid, sodium, cooling, dry kit, and sleep after every one of Gravel Burn's 7 stages. One weather mistake cannot become a week-long recovery deficit. Race-day realities: Hot, exposed semi-desert stages; Seven consecutive days of sun, dust, and recovery demands.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–90g carbs/hour on each of Gravel Burn's 7 event days. Begin recovery fueling within 30 minutes of every finish, replace fluid and sodium, then eat a full carbohydrate-forward meal. Tomorrow's legs are built the night before.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Gravel Burn requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on fast great karoo gravel across a seven-stage point-to-point route to build confidence. Expect: great karoo gravel roads, semi-desert mountain passes, fast non-technical gravel.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Endurance, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 466 miles of fast great karoo gravel across a seven-stage point-to-point route over 7 consecutive days in Great Karoo, Eastern Cape, South Africa.
